description.narrative:
Swedac and SIS will support Ukraine to:
- Maintain the most important aspects of QI (Quality Infrastructure) during the war to sustain trade and vital public services. As a result, it will increase export to the EU during the war.
- Strengthening the Ukrainian QI after the war to promote trade and support a green reconstruction. As a result, the short-term increase of export to EU and investment in export-oriented facilities. These investments will lead to increasing in export in the long term.
- Support the institutions within the QI in Ukraine in their adaptation to, and integration with, the EU. Integrated institutions will increase trust from local investors, as well as from foreign investors. It will lead to rising in long-term investment in export-oriented facilities.

Ukraina är i en EU-närmandeprocess. Kvalitetsinfrastruktur (KI) är en betydelsefull faktor för den ekonomiska integreringen. Swedac och SIS kommer att stödja Ukraina med att upprätthålla de viktigaste aspekterna av KI medan kriget pågår för att upprätthålla handel och viktiga offentliga tjänster; att stärka den ukrainska KI efter kriget för att främja handel och stödja en grön återuppbyggnad; att stödja institutionerna inom KI i Ukraina i deras anpassning till och integration med EU.

Ukraine is in the process of EU integration. Quality infrastructure (QI) is a significant factor in economic integration. Swedac and SIS will support Ukraine to maintain the most important aspects of QI while the war continues to sustain trade and vital public services; strengthening the Ukrainian QI after the war to promote trade and support a green reconstruction; support the institutions within the QI in Ukraine in their adaptation to, and integration with, the EU.

During the year, the project contributed to capacity development in standardisation, accreditation, legal metrology, market surveillance and conformity assessment by supporting the development of the framework for the notifying authority. The support has included trainings, exchange of experience, webinars, roundtable discussions and study visits, which has contributed to increased knowledge of how Swedish and European systems are organised and function in practice. Through these efforts, the project has contributed to:
• Increased knowledge of EU legislation and institutional requirements. • Enhanced capacity of Ukrainian authorities and institutions to translate European Commission recommendations into practical reform measures. • Strengthened coordination among key actors within Ukraine's quality infrastructure
The project has also contributed to maintaining functionality and competence within Ukraine's quality infrastructure during the ongoing war, where factors such as high staff turnover and power outages, with their associated consequences, have affected the authorities ability to carry out their regular activities.
At the same time, the work in 2025 has been characterised by additional challenges. Government reform and institutional restructuring in Ukraine have affected several partner organisations, in some cases delaying planned activities or requiring adjustments to the focus of the work during the year. Despite this, the project has been able to continue through close dialogue with Ukrainian counterparts and a flexible implementation approach.
Overall, the results for the year demonstrate that the project remains relevant and that the support largely corresponds to the needs identified by the Ukrainian partner organisations themselves. In 2025, the project has, in several areas, moved from an initial phase of orientation and trust-building to providing more concrete support for institutional development and EU alignment.
